# The digraph form is what golang.org/x/tools/cmd/digraph reads, so the
# question "which Go line pulled the division slowpath into the kernel" is a
# query rather than a reading of the table. The compiler numbers its
# subroutines, so the node is found by name rather than spelled out.
[!exec:digraph] skip
[!exec:sh] skip
exec sh -c 'cudalineinfo -sass $TESTDATA/fused_layered.sass -ptx $TESTDATA/fused_layered.ptx -format digraph $TESTDATA/fused_layered.json > $WORK/g.txt && digraph somepath main.main "$(digraph nodes < $WORK/g.txt | grep div_rn_noftz_f32_slowpath)" < $WORK/g.txt'
stdout 'main.main main.run'
stdout 'main.attribute main.layered'
# The last edge is a program line calling the subroutine; which of the two
# dividing lines the shortest path runs through is the graph's to choose.
stdout 'kernels.go:(45|50) \$__internal_[0-9]+_\$__cuda_sm3x_div_rn_noftz_f32_slowpath'

# The graph holds the paths that built the unit, so a line no function of
# the program reached through this unit is not on any path to it.
! exec sh -c 'cudalineinfo -sass $TESTDATA/fused_layered.sass -ptx $TESTDATA/fused_layered.ptx -format digraph $TESTDATA/fused_layered.json | digraph somepath main.normalize kernels.go:45'
